title: Webstore - Overview
description: Active users, API traffic, Galera and LDAP per shop node.

panels.title: Logged in now
panels.description: Distinct users with a live session (all nodes).

panels.title: Logged in by node
panels.description: Sessions are tagged with the shop node whose backend issued them. 'unknown' = sessions created before the backend upgrade.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: All traffic through HAProxy on demo-vm.

panels.title: Galera members
panels.description: Cluster size incl. garbd. 3 = both shop nodes + arbitrator.

panels.title: Logged-in users by node
panels.description: Stacked areas per node; the total line should equal their sum.

panels.title: Requests/s by API and node
panels.description: Calls to /api/* routed by HAProxy, split by which shop node served them.

panels.title: Errors/s by API and node
panels.description: 4xx are mostly bad logins / reserved names; 5xx mean a service or dependency failed.

panels.title: Average response time
panels.description: HAProxy rolling average over the last 1024 requests per server.

panels.title: Traffic split (15m)
panels.description: How evenly HAProxy is spreading requests across the shop nodes.

panels.title: Node state
panels.description: Galera is multi-primary: every Synced node accepts reads and writes. There is no fixed primary/secondary.

panels.title: Quorum
panels.description: 'Primary component' = this node is in the majority partition and may serve traffic.

panels.title: Writes accepted (last 5m)
panels.description: Write-sets that originated on each node, i.e. which node the app is actually writing to.

panels.title: Writes accepted per node
panels.description: Each shop node's backend writes to its local MariaDB, so this follows the HAProxy split.

panels.title: Replication pressure
panels.description: Both should sit at 0. A growing queue or paused ratio > 0 means a node can't keep up and Galera is throttling writes cluster-wide.

panels.title: Directory bind
panels.description: Bind as uid=api on each node, exactly like the account/login APIs.

panels.title: Users in ou=People
panels.description: Should match on both nodes once replication catches up.

panels.title: Replication drift
panels.description: Difference in People entries between nodes. Brief non-zero values during sign-ups are normal; a stuck non-zero value means the replication agreement is broken.
